reason: The three one-entry panel proposals describe the same source change, so they rank together: the supplied helper makes the edit feasible, while prior sixteen-call results show no repeatable gain and do not establish transition cost. Scratch reuse and fused packing are source-expressible but need broad assembly and pointer changes, so correctness risk is higher. The three two-K simplification proposals overlap, and the described two-K body is not in the current baseline; any change must first be made distinct from the measured unroll. Packed B adds allocation and copying with unverified benefit. A transpose-aware kernel needs a new generated shape and audit, so it is not currently implementable. No proposal has evidence of reaching 1800 GFLOP/s.
